selection.reason: Bounded matrix carry sequence improved all six row-hash screens by 9.88–15.28%; all independent integer and permutation oracles passed. Selected before complete-proof qualification; the completed result is recorded below.
rejected: expanded NTT factors: mixed timings and added local memory
paired NTT butterflies: regressions on large transforms
fixed NTT columns and geometry: small inconsistent gains and added variants
narrow portable matrix reduction: slower in all six shapes
selection.final_assessment: Retained the V100 matrix carry optimization. All seven aggregation pairs improved: median latency fell 3.35% for four inputs, 3.12% for eight inputs and 3.83% for two concurrent jobs. Native median latency fell 4.34%, with 10/12 paired wins and a 2.99% median within-pair reduction. All 45 targeted tests and 192 fresh benchmark proofs passed. These are bounded V100 fixture measurements with limited sample counts, not production qualification.

proof: The reconstruction carry is added to high>>32, giving floor(S/B^2) <= 20.
B^2 = B-1 modulo p, so add hi*(B-1) to the low word.
If this addition carries, its wrapped value is at most 20*(B-1)-1. Adding B-1 once more is at most 21*(B-1)-1 < 2^64.
Only the already bounded matrix reducer uses this sequence. Canonicalization boundaries are unchanged.
unchanged_callers: fixed internal diagonal: each limb sum below 12*B
arithmetic_bounds.portable_fallback: Exact previous preprocessed code; existing field::source_prefix selects V100 NVIDIA capability 7.0 only.
instruction_review: The full carry chain is inside one asm block, with no function call across condition-code dependencies.
addc.u32 combines the low-word addition carry with high>>32; the proved maximum of 20 fits u32.
Both correction products use mul.wide.u32, retaining all 64 result bits.
The asm output is written after every input has been consumed, so output/input register reuse is safe.

timer_boundaries.four: Aggregation call plus GPU drain; excludes context initialization, artifact output and CPU audit.
timer_boundaries.single: Cohort launch to worker exit; includes initialization, start barrier, aggregation, artifact output and shutdown; excludes CPU audit.
timer_boundaries.concurrent: Cohort launch to last of two worker exits; includes both initializations, start barrier, aggregations, artifact output and shutdown; excludes CPU audits.
timer_boundaries.wallet: Native ABI proving call plus GPU drain; excludes context initialization, buffer setup, artifact output and CPU audit.

limitations: One Tesla V100-PCIE-32GB, fixed aggregation fixtures and bounded resource settings.
Three four-input pairs, two eight-input pairs, two concurrent pairs and twelve native pairs; limited sample counts.
Warmed alternating pairs. First-use profiles and warmups are retained but excluded from the qualification medians.
Both pooled medians and within-pair reductions are reported; short native calls remain sensitive to timing variation.
Kernel event totals and inclusive host spans are not additive; gaps in event coverage do not establish GPU idle time.
No cold-cache, Apple GPU, full-block or production qualification in this run.

references.title: NVIDIA CUDA C++ Best Practices Guide
references.application: Use shared memory for reused data, measure shared-memory and synchronization tradeoffs, and verify complete application performance. Compact and expanded NTT tables are local hypotheses, not vendor performance claims.

references.title: NVIDIA Volta Tuning Guide
references.application: Keep explicit workgroup synchronization between threads sharing data. Volta independent thread scheduling does not justify assuming implicit warp synchronization. Existing launch and memory admission remain enforced.

references.title: NVIDIA PTX ISA 8.5: extended-precision integer arithmetic
references.application: add.cc records carry and addc consumes it. The bounded two-fold Goldilocks sequence and its proof are locally derived; only existing V100-gated code uses the new sequence.
